title: “EDUCATION SUPPORT AND SCHOLARSHIP SCHEMES IN LADAKH”
body_text:
Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Scholarship Division of Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the following ongoing Scholarship Schemes to promote and encourage secondary and higher education amongst ST population in the country, including the UT of Ladakh:
I. Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class IX and X)
II. Post Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class XI and above)
III. National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class)
IV. National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST students (NFST)
V. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students (NOS)
The Scholarship schemes mentioned above at Sl. No. (i) to (ii) are Centrally Sponsored Schemes and implemented through respective States/UTs of the Country. Both Pre & Post Matric Scholarship Schemes are open ended Schemes wherein scholarships are given to all eligible students, without any ceiling limit on the number of selections, for pursuing studies from class 9th to post-Graduation courses whose parental income is not more than Rs. 2.5 lakh per annum. The inviting of applications, verification, selection of beneficiaries and disbursement of scholarship amount is the primary responsibility of the respective States/UTs. Based on the proposals submitted by States/UTs and after examining requisite documents & necessary compliance, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs releases central share of funds to States/UTs. Further, the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations disburse the scholarship amount to all the eligible ST Student's into their bank account through DBT mode.
The Scholarship schemes mentioned above at Sl. No. (iii) to (v) are Central Sector Schemes implemented directly by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. There is no state-wise allocation of funds under these Central Sector Schemes. Under National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students, funds are directly released to the Students/Institutions through DBT mode. The scheme “National Overseas Scholarship for ST students” is implemented through the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the funds are released to ST students studying abroad through Embassies. Based on the vouchers/bills submitted by the MEA regarding payment made by the Embassies to the selected ST students/Institutions, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs reimburse the funds to MEA.
The scheme-wise number of beneficiaries and funds released under all five scholarship schemes for the Union Territory of Ladakh during the last five years is given at Annexure-I.
No such specific assessment has been conducted as on date.
The appraisal and approval process of the Expenditure Finance Commission (EFC) for the continuation of the education related schemes of this Ministry during FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31 is currently ongoing, wherein, inter alia, the proposal to enhance the scope of educational support is included for seeking the approval of the Department of Expenditure on the draft EFC note. The decision on the proposal in the said EFC is subject to the approval of the Competent Authority.
It has been the constant endeavour of the Ministry to ensure pan-India coverage (including in the UT of Ladakh) of all tribal students eligible under various scholarship schemes of this Ministry, by issuing timely advisories and instructions to States and UT Administrations to spread awareness about the schemes in their area.

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed five scholarship schemes run by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for ST students, including in the UT of Ladakh: Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, National Scholarship (Top Class), National Fellowship (NFST), and National Overseas Scholarship (NOS). He explained the Centrally Sponsored vs Central Sector nature of these schemes and their delivery mechanisms, and shared five-year beneficiary and fund-release data for Ladakh via an annexure. He also noted that an Expenditure Finance Commission appraisal for continuing these schemes (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31), including a proposal to enhance educational support, is currently underway.
enrichment.context:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs' scholarship architecture is a key instrument for Scheduled Tribe (ST) educational upliftment, structured across two funding models: Centrally Sponsored Schemes (Pre-Matric and Post-Matric, jointly funded and implemented via States/UTs with central share released after compliance checks) and Central Sector Schemes (Top Class, NFST, NOS, funded and implemented directly by the Union government via DBT, with NOS routed through Indian missions abroad via the MEA). This bifurcation reflects the broader Centre-State cooperative federalism model used across many social sector schemes in India, where the Centre sets norms and releases funds while states handle ground-level implementation, verification and disbursal.

Ladakh, as a Union Territory carved out in 2019 (following abrogation of Article 370) with a substantial tribal population (many communities like Balti, Beda, Bot, Brokpa, Changpa, Garra, Mon, Purigpa are notified as STs), is a focus area for ensuring these welfare schemes reach remote, high-altitude, sparsely populated regions. The data shows fluctuating beneficiary numbers over FY2020-21 to FY2025-26 with no clear upward trend, and negligible uptake of the National Overseas Scholarship (0-1 beneficiaries most years), highlighting persistent outreach and awareness challenges in far-flung UTs. The mention of an ongoing EFC appraisal for FY2026-31 signals that scheme design, funding norms, and coverage may be revised soon, reflecting periodic government review of centrally sponsored welfare schemes' financial sustainability and effectiveness (as mandated for continuation past a Finance Commission cycle).

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following scholarship schemes for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students is implemented through the Ministry of External Affairs and Indian Embassies abroad?
options: National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST Students (NFST)
National Overseas Scholarship for ST Students (NOS)
National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST Students (Top Class)
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) for ST students is implemented through the Ministry of External Affairs, with funds released to students via Indian Embassies, and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs later reimburses MEA based on vouchers.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, which of the following statements is correct?
options: They are Central Sector Schemes with no role for State/UT Governments
They are open-ended schemes with no ceiling on the number of selections for eligible students
Only students with parental income above Rs 2.5 lakh per annum are eligible
They are implemented directly by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs without involving States/UTs
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states both Pre- and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are open-ended Centrally Sponsored Schemes with no ceiling on selections, for students whose parental income does not exceed Rs 2.5 lakh per annum, implemented through States/UTs.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of centrally sponsored scholarship schemes in promoting educational access among Scheduled Tribe populations in remote Union Territories like Ladakh. What are the challenges in ensuring their effective implementation?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance and Welfare Schemes

mains_questions.question: Examine the Centre-State institutional mechanism involved in the implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes, using the example of ST scholarship schemes, and suggest measures to improve last-mile delivery in geographically challenging regions.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Centre-State Relations and Governance
